title: The component locus of a smooth section is open
statement: Let $g:P\to T$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes, and let $\sigma:T\to P$ satisfy $g\circ\sigma=\mathrm{id}_T$. For $p\in P$, let $C_p$ be the connected component of $\sigma(g(p))$ in the subspace $g^{-1}(\{g(p)\})$. Then $\{p\in P\mid p\in C_p\}$ is open in $P$.

proof.text: Apply local constructibility of the relative section component (Stacks 055P). Smoothness supplies the locally finite presentation instance required by that theorem.
Apply stability under generalization of the smooth section component, the generic-point part of Stacks 055Q.

For a point p choose its affine-cover chart j and a preimage q. Pull local constructibility and generalization stability back along j. The chart is a quasi-compact, quasi-separated prespectral space, so its locally constructible subset is constructible. Apply Mathlib PrimeSpectrum.isOpen_of_stableUnderGeneralization_of_isConstructible. The open immersion j maps this open preimage to an open neighbourhood of p contained in the component locus. The neighbourhood criterion for openness finishes the proof.

proof_origin.place: Tags 055P and 055Q; affine topological criterion Tag 00I0
proof_origin.note: Q3 decomposes the algebraic argument into local constructibility and generalization stability; the complete Lean combination uses affine-cover neighbourhoods and Mathlib. The unit still uses the relative connected component open in the slicing construction.
